facts: This appeal has been filed under Section 379 CrPC and Section 2 of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970.

The five appellants before us are the original Accused 1, 2, 3, 8 and 10. They along with others were tried by the Sessions Judge, Narsinghpur for the offences punishable under Section 148 and 302 read with Section 149 IPC.

The prosecution relied on the evidence of the three eyewitnesses but the learned Sessions Judge acquitted all of them holding that there are certain discrepancies in the version of the eyewitnesses and therefore they are unreliable.
The deceased Halke was said to be a goonda addicted to liquor and in the state of intoxication used to beat villagers. Appellant 1 was one such victim.
After inflicting injuries the accused left. PW 1 went away from the village to a nearby village where he met on Kanhaiya and narrated the incident to him.
The Police Officer, PW 14 registered the crime, went to the scene of occurrence, held inquest and sent the dead body for post-mortem.
The doctor, who conducted the post-mortem, found 20 injuries. He also found the fracture of the left temple bone, pressure on the brain and hemorrhage.
He opined that the death was due to shock and hemorrhage as a result of those injuries.
issues: Whether the evidence of the three eyewitnesses is reliable
Whether the discrepancies in their evidence are material
petitioner_arguments: The plea of the accused in one of denial
The prosecution mainly relied on the evidence of PWs 1, 2, 3 and 7
There is no evidence to show that theses three eyewitnesses should be inimical towards the accused
The discrepancies pointed out are frivolous
respondent_arguments: The High Court has rightly pointed out that discrepancies pointed out are frivolous
The names of the rest of the persons were mentioned even at the earliest stage
This was a supporting factor which according to the leaned Judges lent assurance so far those four accused were concerned
court_reasoning: It is evidence that these witness are not of same caste as of the deceased and nor in any way related to him. They are, however, related to the servant engaged by the deceased.

A witness in normally considered to be an independent witness unless he springs from the sources which are likely to be tainted such as enmity or relationship and which make him inclined to implicate the accused falsely
Nothing has been shown as to why these three eyewitnesses should be inimical towards the accused
The High Court, however, was prepared to accept the evidence of the eyewitnesses only in respect of the appellants

In this view of the matter we give the benefit of doubt to Todal, A 8. We are of the view that the remaining four appellants along with some others i.e. more than five persons participated in the occurrence
holding: The appeal is allowed so far as Todal, A 8 is concerned and dismissed so far as other appellants are concerned
The bail bond of Todal A 8 stands cancelled
The other appellants shall surrender to serve out the sentences
